findings.title: Shard splitting applies template variables and ad-hoc filters twice
findings.body: runSplitQuery now maps every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables(..., request.filters) before executing. runShardSplitQuery does the same before grouping, then builds each shard sub-request from those already interpolated targets and calls runSplitQuery. On the shard-splitting path template application therefore runs twice per target (once up front, then once per shard group inside runSplitQuery). applyTemplateVariables is not idempotent: its contract appends ad-hoc filters to the LogQL expression, so the second call inserts the same matchers again, for example {app="foo", env="prod", __stream_shard__=~"1|2", env="prod"}. Loki rejects duplicate label matchers, so dashboards with ad-hoc filters and shard splitting fail or change query meaning. A variable value that itself contains $ or ${...} is expanded again on the second pass and can be corrupted. The updated shard test expects applyTemplateVariables to be called 5 times for a single target (1 initial call plus 1 per shard group), which locks in the double application. Interpolate once for sharding decisions in runShardSplitQuery, and do not call applyTemplateVariables again in runSplitQuery on targets that are already interpolated (or strip filters from the sub-request so they cannot be reapplied).

findings.title: $__auto is not resolved before splitting; the new test only stubs it
findings.body: The new tests claim a query such as count_over_time({a="b"}[$__auto]) is interpolated to a concrete range before split execution, but they only pass because createLokiDatasource is given a templateSrv.replace stub that string-replaces $__auto. $__auto is a Loki query macro, not a Grafana template variable, and TemplateSrv.replace does not define it. The only interpolation this PR adds is applyTemplateVariables, which leaves $__auto in the expression. It is still resolved later by the Loki backend (the same step path calculateStep says it replicates from pkg/tsdb/loki/step.go) or by runQuery, using each sub-request's split time range. Chunks therefore still get a step derived from the chunk instead of the original range, which is the failure mode early interpolation is supposed to prevent. The unit test cannot catch that because the stub removes $__auto before runQuery is observed. Substitute $__auto from the original request range before partitioning, and do not fake that substitution in templateSrv.replace.
